PullRequest.Title: sessions: add Dev Container workspace menu option
PullRequest.Body: ## Summary - add a native side-chevron submenu to eligible local workspace-picker folders - route **Use Dev Container** through the existing Agent Host draft preference flow - label the selected workspace as ` - Dev Container`, including its ARIA label - document the workflow in Agents accessibility help and cover availability gating/selection in unit tests Fixes #335302 ## Validation - `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionWorkspacePicker.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.test.ts` (110 passing) - targeted `npm run eslint -- ...` for all changed TypeScript files - `npm run hygiene` - `git diff --check`

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The per-promise callback, visibility guard, force-reopen path, and synchronous ActionList/DOM/layout implementations are directly visible. The exact frame cost varies, but N successful results deterministically cause N full popup rebuilds.
Findings.PerformanceResource: ActionList objects, popup DOM nodes, event listeners, and synchronous layout work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Every local recent whose availability resolves true independently invokes showPicker(true); with N configured recent folders resolving while the picker remains open, the entire up-to-20-row popup is torn down and rebuilt N times in quick succession.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: repeated synchronous popup reconstruction and layout, causing picker jank
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, opening the workspace picker constructed and laid out the popup once; no asynchronous per-row availability completion could force additional popup recreations.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each successful availability promise now immediately force-reopens the visible picker instead of batching results or updating the affected list row.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 1895-1897 newly call showPicker(true, ...) independently from each availability promise's then callback.
Findings.Title: Coalesce availability-driven picker refreshes
Findings.Impact: Users with several Dev Container projects in recent workspaces can incur a burst of full list allocations, DOM teardown/recreation, focus work, and layout just after opening the menu, producing visible jank and unnecessary CPU/GC pressure.
Findings.Evidence: Line 1896 calls showPicker(true) from every successful promise completion. showPicker sees an already-visible picker and calls _hidePicker before _showFlatPicker/_showTabbedPicker. The flat path creates a new ActionList and ActionWidgetService._renderWidget calls layout and focus; the tabbed path creates a new ActionList and reads offsetHeight during layout. The platform already exposes ActionWidgetService.updateItems and TabbedActionListWidget.refreshActiveList for in-place refresh, but this path reconstructs the popup once per completion.
Findings.Recommendation: Aggregate or debounce availability completions and refresh the visible list once, preferably using updateItems/refreshActiveList (or patching the resolved row) rather than hiding and recreating the popup.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed loop, hard list caps, cache reset, provider delegation, and exact two-stat/IPC implementation are directly traced. Magnitude varies with the number and storage location of local recents, but the new boundary cardinality and repeated-open trigger are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem existence checks and shared-process IPC calls
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each picker open starts one availability request for every visible local recent workspace (up to 20 after the service combines 10 session recents and 10 VS Code recents); each request performs two fileService.exists operations, and configured folders also issue an isDockerAvailable IPC call. The loop starts them without a limiter, and the cache is cleared on every fresh open.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive filesystem and IPC activity whenever the workspace picker is opened
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, opening the workspace picker only built the recent-workspace list; Dev Container availability was checked once for the workspace when a draft was created, not for every recent folder.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added call inside the recent-workspace loop probes Dev Container availability for every local row, and showPicker clears the probe cache whenever the popup is freshly opened. Selecting a row then still creates a draft whose existing _resolveDevContainerAvailability path probes the selected workspace again.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1470 newly invokes _isDevContainerWorkspaceAvailable from inside the recent-workspace loop; RIGHT lines 624-626 clear the cache at each fresh picker opening, making the fan-out recur.
Findings.Title: Cache or lazily validate Dev Container availability
Findings.Impact: Opening the picker with a populated local history now launches up to 40 concurrent filesystem stats plus IPC roundtrips; slow disks or file-scheme network folders can generate an I/O burst on a routine UI interaction, and the selected folder is immediately re-statted during draft creation.
Findings.Evidence: _buildItems iterates the merged recentWorkspaces and line 1470 calls _isDevContainerWorkspaceAvailable for each local row. That helper calls provider.isDevContainerWorkspaceAvailable, which delegates to IDevContainerAgentHostService.isAvailable; isDevContainerWorkspaceAvailable in devContainerAgentHostConnector.contribution.ts awaits two fileService.exists calls and then mainService.isDockerAvailable. SessionsRecentWorkspacesService caps each of its own and VS Code lists at 10 but returns their deduplicated combination, while showPicker clears _devContainerAvailability on every fresh open. LocalAgentHostSessionsProvider.createNewSession separately retains the pre-existing per-selected-workspace availability check.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep availability results across picker opens and invalidate them from bounded provider/configuration/file-change signals, or defer the check to the row/submenu the user interacts with. Also share/coalesce the selected workspace's result with draft creation so the required final validation does not duplicate the same stats.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the new-session workspace picker with local recent workspaces
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first popup render is synchronous and does not await Dev Container probes, so availability I/O is off the initial-open critical path. Showing each Dev Container submenu waits for that row's probe, and every successful completion synchronously force-rebuilds the visible popup on the UI path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two concurrent exists calls per visible local recent, up to 40 calls per picker open after recents caps and deduplication
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Picker opening performed no Dev Container filesystem availability checks; only draft creation checked its selected workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial popup render path, but gates submenu appearance and consumes I/O during interaction

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call shared-process mainService.isDockerAvailable for each folder that has a configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per configured local recent; node-side executable resolution is shared by a cached Promise
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Docker-availability IPC was initiated by opening the picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off initial popup rendering but gates submenu availability and contributes to the completion burst

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The deduplicated local subset of up to 10 session recents plus 10 VS Code recents (maximum effective cardinality 20); configured folders among that subset control refresh count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The loop launches all availability requests without a limiter. Each request launches its two file-existence checks in Promise.all, yielding up to 40 concurrent filesystem operations; configured candidates independently issue IPC and independently trigger popup refreshes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Promise/boolean entries coalesce duplicate builds while one popup remains open, and the node-side Docker executable check is process-cached. The picker cache is explicitly cleared on every fresh open, so all per-folder filesystem checks and IPC requests recur; selecting a folder does not share this cache with draft creation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: loop cardinality, cache reset, exact boundary calls, concurrency, and force-rebuild call path were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most users have fewer than 20 local recents and fewer configured Dev Container projects; disk/network latency and exact popup layout cost vary. The maximum cardinality and repeated-open/rebuild behavior are code-established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff adds repeated per-recent boundary fan-out and uncoalesced full popup rebuilds on a routine UI interaction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose Use Dev Container, create the draft, and send the first request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The menu selection creates/replaces a draft through the existing session flow. Draft creation independently rechecks availability. When worktree isolation is currently selected and combined mode is disabled, the new normalization waits for config resolution and applies folder isolation; tracked config work must settle before session preparation/send. Dev Container connection/preparation remains on the existing first-send path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeat the selected workspace's two Dev Container configuration existence checks during LocalAgentHostSessionsProvider.createNewSession
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two checks once for the selected draft, in addition to the same two checks newly performed when the picker opened
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This one-workspace draft check already existed; the diff adds the earlier picker check, causing duplication across the workflow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Availability must resolve before pending Dev Container preference can become enabled, though draft construction proceeds asynchronously

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve changed isolation config with the Agent Host when worktree must be normalized to folder
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one config update/resolution per enablement when isolation equals worktree
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed checkbox disabled Dev Container enablement while incompatible worktree isolation was selected, so users had to make the equivalent config change manually.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Tracked configuration operation must settle before preparation; this preserves the prior incompatibility rule that previously required the user to change isolation

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect/prepare the Dev Container Agent Host and resolve target session configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected workspace connection, coalesced by existing active/pending connection maps; target config values are applied sequentially as before
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Dev Container preparation path ran after enabling the prior checkbox.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected workspace and one active draft; normalization performs at most one isolation update for the selection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The selected workspace's draft availability check can overlap other setup, while normalization is sequenced behind current config resolution. Dev Container connection remains singular/coalesced by the existing connection service.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The picker availability result is not reused, so draft creation repeats two file checks and an IPC request for the selected workspace. Docker executable detection itself is warm after the first node-side check. Existing connection maps coalesce connection creation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for duplicated availability checks and normalization sequencing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent-host config resolution and container startup duration vary, but their cardinality and ordering are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: The duplicated selected-workspace availability work supports the boundary-fanout finding. The one-time isolation normalization is behavior-preserving for a previously disallowed combination and is not separately reportable.

Scenarios.Scenario: Update configuration on the active Agent Host draft while the composer remains visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every matching onDidChangeSessionConfig event synchronously resynchronizes workspace-picker mode and presentation. This resolves the selected folder from bounded recents/providers and updates trigger state, but does not cross filesystem, IPC, database, subprocess, or network boundaries.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active draft; event frequency follows initial config resolution and user config changes. Recent lookup is bounded by at most 20 merged entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event handlers run synchronously; provider config resolution itself remains sequenced by existing provider logic.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new external cache is consulted. Recent workspaces and provider resolution are in-memory; no availability cache is cleared by this synchronization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added event listener and _selectFolder call path were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of config pulses varies by provider and user changes, but synchronous work is bounded and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate report: the added in-memory work is bounded, and no concrete user-visible performance degradation is established.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all 13 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted two findings: repeated per-recent Dev Container filesystem/IPC fan-out caused by per-open cache invalidation, and uncoalesced full popup reconstruction for each successful availability result. No concrete shipped-regression fix qualified for blame/report_regression_fix.
